</section>
<section id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Per-Noise-Level memorization.</h5>

<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Motivated by the definition above, we identify a finer-grained notion of memorization at each noise level <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.
Given a training set <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> sampled from a population distribution <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>, a denoiser <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m^{\bullet}_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi><mo>∙</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m^{\bullet}_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> is said to have memorized <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math> at a noise level <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> if for (nearly) all sample test points <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{\text{test}}\sim p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub><mo>∼</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{\text{test}}\sim p</annotation></semantics></math> and a large portion of noise samples <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝒁</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(m_{\sigma}^{\bullet}(x_{\text{test}}+\sigma\bm{Z}))&lt;d_{2\mathrm{NN}}(m_{\sigma}^{\bullet}(x_{\text{test}}+\sigma\bm{Z}))/3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi><mo>∙</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝒁</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi><mo>∙</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝒁</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(m_{\sigma}^{\bullet}(x_{\text{test}}+\sigma\bm{Z}))&lt;d_{2\mathrm{NN}}(m_{\sigma}^{\bullet}(x_{\text{test}}+\sigma\bm{Z}))/3</annotation></semantics></math>. Under this notion we can examine denoiser performance at a specific noise level.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">With these two metrics, we now analyze where memorization arises for <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span> and <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-50K</span>. As expected and shown in <a href="#S3.T1" title="In Trajectory-Level memorization. ‣ 3 Empirical Investigation of Memorization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Table</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span> exhibits strong trajectory-level memorization (92.2% of samples), while <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-50K</span> generalizes well (0% memorization); we omit <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EMP-1K</span>, which is expected to exhibit 100% memorization. We now examine per-noise-level memorization across the three models. Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3 Empirical Investigation of Memorization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows that <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-50K</span> exhibits no memorization for any <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, whereas <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EMP-1K</span> increasingly approaches nearest-neighbor behavior as <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\!\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0.108em" stretchy="false">↓</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\!\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>, reaching <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx 100\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mn>100</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx 100\%</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma&lt;0.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma&lt;0.3</annotation></semantics></math>.
In contrast, <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span> attains its highest memorization rate in an intermediate regime (peaking at <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim 26\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mn>26</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim 26\%</annotation></semantics></math> around <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\in[1.1,5.3]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1.1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5.3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\in[1.1,5.3]</annotation></semantics></math>) and drops to nearly <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> memorization rate at very small <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. We include qualitative visualizations of one-step denoising outputs across different noise levels in Appendix <a href="#A5.SS7" title="E.7 One-Step Memorization Showcase ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.7</span></a>, which further illustrate this phenomenon.
In summary, while both <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span> and <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EMP-1K</span> exhibit strong trajectory-level memorization, the diffusion model behind <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span> in fact deviates significantly from the empirical optimal <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EMP-1K</span>. In particular, the per-noise-level memorization behaviors are quite different from mid-to-small levels of <math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>s.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we would like to investigate how per-noise-level memorization affects the trajectory-level memorization. We conduct the <em id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">denoiser swapping experiments</em> (Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Trajectory-Level memorization. ‣ 3 Empirical Investigation of Memorization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, see Appendix <a href="#A5.SS6" title="E.6 Denoiser Swapping Experiments ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.6</span></a> for details) which show that swapping the denoiser in the medium region (<math id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\in[0.14,8.4]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0.14</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8.4</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\in[0.14,8.4]</annotation></semantics></math>) flips memorization behavior.
Specifically, replacing <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span> with <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-50K</span> in the medium region drops memorization from 92.2% to 0%, while the reverse (swapping <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-50K</span>’s denoiser with <span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span>’s in this range) increases it from 0% to 92.2%. In contrast, swapping in large or small regions has negligible effect.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Taken together, these results reveal a qualitative mismatch between empirical optimality (<span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EMP-1K</span>) and learned memorization (<span id="S3.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span>): while the empirical optimal memorizes strongly across a broad noise range, the learned diffusion model memorizes primarily in an intermediate regime. This suggests that to fully understand memorization in diffusion models, we not only need to analyze the trajectory-level behavior but also the per-noise-level contributions. In particular, if one wants to mitigate memorization, it is crucial to understand and control the denoiser behavior at per-noise-level, especially in the medium noise regime.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S3" title="3 Empirical Investigation of Memorization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows that per-noise-level memorization concentrates at medium noise levels and contributes most to trajectory-level memorization (as shown by the denoiser swapping experiments in Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Trajectory-Level memorization. ‣ 3 Empirical Investigation of Memorization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). In this section, we seek to provide a geometric interpretation of this phenomenon. In particular, we characterize the three regimes and explain why the two ends are “calm” while the middle is “wild”. We further identify a “danger zone” of memorization risk in the medium noise regime and provide a practical mitigation strategy in <a href="#S5" title="5 Targeted Noise Region Undertraining ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Key Players for Per-Noise-Level Memorizations</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To analyze per-noise-level memorization we examine the training loss <a href="#S2.E1" title="In Training. ‣ 2 Background ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqn.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> when <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is fixed, which reduces to <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{MSE}_{\sigma}(p_{\mathcal{D}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>MSE</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{MSE}_{\sigma}(p_{\mathcal{D}})</annotation></semantics></math> (cf. <a href="#S3.E5" title="In 3 Empirical Investigation of Memorization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqn.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).
Two major players arise from this loss: the empirical optimal denoiser <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math>,
which the model attempts to fit, and the distribution of noisy training samples <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math>, which determines the supervised region. With sufficient model capacity, the trained denoiser <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{\sigma}^{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi><mi>θ</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{\sigma}^{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math> can match <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> on this region; but if this supervision is not of sufficient coverage of test samples, the trained denoiser might not generalize beyond that. Consequently, whether this induces per-noise-level memorization depends on how these two players interact as the noise level varies.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To understand these two players, we analyze two quantities below: the <em id="S4.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">posterior weight</em>, induced from the empirical optimal denoiser, and the so-called <em id="S4.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Gaussian shell coverage</em>,
induced from the distribution of training samples. Their combined behavior</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">at different noise levels leads to our characterization of three distinct noise regimes (cf. <a href="#S4.SS2" title="4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Posterior Weight.</span> Recall that the functions <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{i}(x,\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{i}(x,\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> defined in <a href="#S2.E3" title="In Optimal solution. ‣ 2 Background ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqn.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>
are the posterior weights
on the data samples <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> at a noise level <math id="S4.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. From <a href="#S2.E2" title="In Optimal solution. ‣ 2 Background ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqn.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> it is clear that the posterior weights determine how close the empirical optimal denoiser is to a given data point. In particular if at a given noise level one weight is always substantially larger than the rest, the empirical optimal denoiser becomes concentrated near the corresponding data points, resulting in per-noise-level memorization of the training data. As a trained model attempts to fit the empirical optimal denoiser, it is worth investigating which noise levels yield this effect. To make this more precise, we define the following quantity.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 4.1</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The <em id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">posterior weight for the dataset <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}=\{x_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}=\{x_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math></em> at a noise level <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is given by the quantity</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\sigma}(\mathcal{D}):=\mathbb{E}_{\begin{subarray}{c}\bm{X}\sim p_{\mathcal{D}}\\
\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})\end{subarray}}\max_{1\leq i\leq N}w_{i}(\bm{X}_{\sigma},\sigma)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mtable rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></msub></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mi>𝒁</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><munder><mi>max</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></munder><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\sigma}(\mathcal{D}):=\mathbb{E}_{\begin{subarray}{c}\bm{X}\sim p_{\mathcal{D}}\\
\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})\end{subarray}}\max_{1\leq i\leq N}w_{i}(\bm{X}_{\sigma},\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Note that we only take expectation over the training data. This is due to the fact that during training, the model only has access to <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S4.SS1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝑿</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}</annotation></semantics></math> is drawn from the training data distribution.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">This definition captures the expected maximum posterior weight over all noisy samples at a given noise level sigma. This quantity can be easily estimated on a given dataset; see e.g., <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, where we graph a curve of the weight using the CIFAR-10 dataset. The figure shows an interesting sharp transition window at moderate noise levels which we aim to provide a theoretical explanation next.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">First of all, consider any sample data point, and w.l.o.g, assume we consider <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}\in\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}\in\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math>. Although the maximum weight <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max_{i}w_{i}(x_{1}+\sigma\bm{Z},\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>max</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝒁</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max_{i}w_{i}(x_{1}+\sigma\bm{Z},\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> is present in the definition above, this maximum is usually attained at moderate noise levels for <math id="S4.SS1.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., the maximum is attained at the data point itself. See <a href="#A5.F7" title="In E.3 Max vs Self Posterior Weight ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> for an empirical validation, where the two quantities are compared across a full noise schedule.
For this reason we provide the following theorem that gives noise thresholds for high probability weight concentration.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 4.2</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}\in\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}\in\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math> and condition on <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}=x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}=x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{1}(\bm{X}_{\sigma},\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{1}(\bm{X}_{\sigma},\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the posterior weight on <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> at a noise level <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. Then for any <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q\in(\frac{1}{2},1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q\in(\frac{1}{2},1)</annotation></semantics></math>, with probability at least <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, we have that:</span></p>
<ul id="S4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I1.ix1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.ix1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.ix1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.ix1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If
</span><math id="S4.I1.ix1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\geq\min_{K&gt;1}\frac{d_{K\mathrm{NN}}(x_{1})}{a_{K-1,\delta,q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>NN</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub></mfrac></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\geq\min_{K&gt;1}\frac{d_{K\mathrm{NN}}(x_{1})}{a_{K-1,\delta,q}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.ix1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">,
then </span><math id="S4.I1.ix1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{1}(\bm{X}_{\sigma},\sigma)\leq q." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{1}(\bm{X}_{\sigma},\sigma)\leq q.</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.ix2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.ix2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If
</span><math id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\leq\frac{d_{2\mathrm{NN}}(x_{1})}{b_{\delta,q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\leq\frac{d_{2\mathrm{NN}}(x_{1})}{b_{\delta,q}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">,
then </span><math id="S4.I1.ix2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{1}(\bm{X}_{\sigma},\sigma)\geq q." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{1}(\bm{X}_{\sigma},\sigma)\geq q.</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where the constants <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{K,\delta,q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{K,\delta,q}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{\delta,q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{\delta,q}</annotation></semantics></math> are defined by</span></p>
<table id="S4.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle a_{K,\delta,q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>a</mi><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle a_{K,\delta,q}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle:=F^{-1}(\delta/K)+\sqrt{\left(F^{-1}(\delta/K)\right)^{2}+2\log\left(\frac{Kq}{1-q}\right)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle:=F^{-1}(\delta/K)+\sqrt{\left(F^{-1}(\delta/K)\right)^{2}+2\log\left(\frac{Kq}{1-q}\right)}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
