<tbody id="S4.Ex3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle b_{\delta,q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle b_{\delta,q}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle:=\tilde{F}^{-1}(\delta/N)+\sqrt{\left(\tilde{F}^{-1}(\delta/N)\right)^{2}+2\log\left(\frac{Nq}{1-q}\right)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>F</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mrow><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>F</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>/</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle:=\tilde{F}^{-1}(\delta/N)+\sqrt{\left(\tilde{F}^{-1}(\delta/N)\right)^{2}+2\log\left(\frac{Nq}{1-q}\right)}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">and where <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> is the CDF of the standard normal distribution and <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{F}:=1-F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>F</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{F}:=1-F</annotation></semantics></math>. (Note that <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(x_{1})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(x_{1})=0</annotation></semantics></math>.)</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Remark 4.3</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We consider a dataset consisting of 1K images randomly sampled from the CIFAR-10 dataset. Using the bounds given by <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 4.2. ‣ 4.1 Key Players for Per-Noise-Level Memorizations ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>, over a random sample of 20 points, the average lower bound
needed to guarantee posterior concentration below <math id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.6</annotation></semantics></math> with probability <math id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.95</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.95</annotation></semantics></math> was <math id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\geq 22.54" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>22.54</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\geq 22.54</annotation></semantics></math>. The average upper bound needed to guarantee posterior concentration above <math id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.95</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.95</annotation></semantics></math> with probability <math id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.95</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.95</annotation></semantics></math> was <math id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\leq 2.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>2.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\leq 2.25</annotation></semantics></math>. This upper bound compares well with <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, where in the same setting <math id="S4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma=2.25" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2.25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma=2.25</annotation></semantics></math> lies close to where the curve of the average max weight reaches 0.95.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Remark 4.4</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Section <a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 Cosine Similarity Concentration ‣ Appendix A Posterior Concentration and Cosine Similarity Concentration ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a> we use a variant of <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 4.2. ‣ 4.1 Key Players for Per-Noise-Level Memorizations ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> to theoretically explain the sharp alignment between the optimal and conditional vector fields observed in high dimensional flow matching settings by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.SS1.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Gaussian Shell Coverage.</span>
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>]</cite> proposes using Gaussian shells around training data points to model supervised regions during training. Following their intuition, we will use a theoretically tighter bound of Gaussian shells (cf. <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma 4.5 (Gaussian concentration []). ‣ 4.1 Key Players for Per-Noise-Level Memorizations ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>) and propose a novel notion of data coverage utilizing the supervised regions via Gaussian shells.
The following high dimensional concentration result is key to our analysis in this paper (see proof in <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Gaussian Shell and Coverage ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Appendix</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 4.5</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Gaussian concentration <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>)<span id="S4.Thmtheorem5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math> and fix <math id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. Define
<math id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d}:=\sqrt{d-2\sqrt{cd}}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>in</mi></msubsup><mo>:=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d}:=\sqrt{d-2\sqrt{cd}},</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}:=\sqrt{d+2\sqrt{cd}+2c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>out</mi></msubsup><mo>:=</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msqrt><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}:=\sqrt{d+2\sqrt{cd}+2c}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐙</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})</annotation></semantics></math>. Then,
<math id="S4.Thmtheorem5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{P}\big(\|\bm{Z}\|\in[r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d},r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}]\big)\geq 1-2e^{-c}." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝐙</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>in</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>out</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{P}\big(\|\bm{Z}\|\in[r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d},r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}]\big)\geq 1-2e^{-c}.</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">This result states that <math id="S4.SS1.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})</annotation></semantics></math> will concentrate in a thin shell around the origin with radius <math id="S4.SS1.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\approx\sqrt{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≈</mo><msqrt><mi>d</mi></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\approx\sqrt{d}</annotation></semantics></math> and thickness controlled by <math id="S4.SS1.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>. If we let <math id="S4.SS1.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=5</annotation></semantics></math>, then the concentration probability is at least 0.9865. So we will simply let <math id="S4.SS1.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=5</annotation></semantics></math> through this paper unless otherwise stated.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p10.1" class="ltx_p">Based on the concentration result, for any <math id="S4.SS1.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.SS1.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, we define the
<em id="S4.SS1.p10.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Gaussian shell</em> centered at <math id="S4.SS1.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> by</p>
<table id="S4.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\sigma}({x}):=\Bigl\{x^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}:\sigma r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d}\leq\|x^{\prime}-x\|\leq\sigma r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}\Bigr\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>in</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>out</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\sigma}({x}):=\Bigl\{x^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}:\sigma r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d}\leq\|x^{\prime}-x\|\leq\sigma r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}\Bigr\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p11.1" class="ltx_p">As a direct consequence of <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma 4.5 (Gaussian concentration []). ‣ 4.1 Key Players for Per-Noise-Level Memorizations ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>, we have that</p>
<table id="S4.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{P}\big(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in S_{\sigma}({x})\mid\bm{X}=x\big)\geq\ 1-2e^{-c}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mn> 1</mn><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{P}\big(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in S_{\sigma}({x})\mid\bm{X}=x\big)\geq\ 1-2e^{-c}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p11.2" class="ltx_p">This shows that a single Gaussian shell provides a high-probability description of where a noisy data point lies. Based on the notion of Gaussian shells, we next introduce the notion of data coverage.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 4.6</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Gaussian Shell Coverage)<span id="S4.Thmtheorem6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Suppose <math id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}=\{x_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}=\{x_{i}\}_{i=1}^{N}</annotation></semantics></math> is a finite dataset sampled from the data distribution <math id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>. We define the <em id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Gaussian shell coverage</em> of the distribution <math id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> relative to <math id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}</annotation></semantics></math> at the noise level <math id="S4.Thmtheorem6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> as follows:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\sigma}(p,\mathcal{D}):=\mathbb{P}\left(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in\bigcup_{i=1}^{N}S_{\sigma}({x_{i}})\right),\quad\text{where }\bm{X}\sim p" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">∈</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">⋃</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mtext>where </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝑿</mi></mrow><mo>∼</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\sigma}(p,\mathcal{D}):=\mathbb{P}\left(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in\bigcup_{i=1}^{N}S_{\sigma}({x_{i}})\right),\quad\text{where }\bm{X}\sim p</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p12.1" class="ltx_p">The quantity approximately quantifies the likelihood that a diffusion model encounters a noisy test <math id="S4.SS1.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{\text{test}}+\sigma z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mtext>test</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{\text{test}}+\sigma z</annotation></semantics></math> during training. In other words, <math id="S4.SS1.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> measures how large a portion of the underlying ground-truth distribution is covered by the training set after the convolution <math id="S4.SS1.p12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\sigma}=p*\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}I)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∗</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\sigma}=p*\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2}I)</annotation></semantics></math>. For brevity, in the remainder of the paper we will refer to the Gaussian shell coverage <math id="S4.SS1.p12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\sigma}(p,\mathcal{D})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\sigma}(p,\mathcal{D})</annotation></semantics></math> simply as “coverage” when no confusion can arise.
Note that while in applications the data distribution <math id="S4.SS1.p12.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is not known, this quantity can be empirically estimated if a test dataset is available; see <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> where we estimate <math id="S4.SS1.p12.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> for the CIFAR-10 dataset.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p13.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> also exhibits an interesting sharp phase transition for the coverage as the noise level varies.
To provide a theoretical understanding why this happens, we find it better to treat the dataset as random and study the coverage in expectation.
Interestingly, it turns out that controlling this coverage is closely related to the probability mass of intersection between just two shells. Below we provide a clean description of such a probability mass.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 4.7</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S4.Thmtheorem7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e_{1}=[1,0,\cdots,0]^{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋯</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e_{1}=[1,0,\cdots,0]^{T}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> and define</p>
<table id="S4.Ex6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi_{d,c}\left(t\right):=\mathbb{P}\!\left(\|\bm{Z}\|,\left\|\bm{Z}+te_{1}\right\|\in[r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d},r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}]\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.441em;" width="0.441em"><mi>ℙ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝒁</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝒁</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>‖</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>in</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>out</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{d,c}\left(t\right):=\mathbb{P}\!\left(\|\bm{Z}\|,\left\|\bm{Z}+te_{1}\right\|\in[r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d},r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}]\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p14" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p14.1" class="ltx_p">The function <math id="S4.SS1.p14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi_{d,c}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{d,c}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> measures the probability of a Gaussian noisy observation for one data point lying also in the Gaussian shell over a data point at distance <math id="S4.SS1.p14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> and hence roughly represents the “probability of seeing a noisy data in the intersection of two Gaussian shells”.
The following result shows that the coverage is closely controlled by <math id="S4.SS1.p14.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi_{d,c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{d,c}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 4.8</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X},\bm{X}_{1},\dots,\bm{X}_{N}\overset{\text{i.i.d.}}{\sim}p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mo>∼</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic" mathsize="0.700em">i.i.d.</mtext></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X},\bm{X}_{1},\dots,\bm{X}_{N}\overset{\text{i.i.d.}}{\sim}p</annotation></semantics></math>, and let <math id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐙</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})</annotation></semantics></math> be independent of <math id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\bm{X},\bm{X}_{1},\dots,\bm{X}_{N})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\bm{X},\bm{X}_{1},\dots,\bm{X}_{N})</annotation></semantics></math>. Fix a noise level <math id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. Define the union of shells
<math id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{U}_{\sigma}:=\bigcup_{i=1}^{N}S_{\sigma}({\bm{X}_{i}})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">:=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>⋃</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>N</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{U}_{\sigma}:=\bigcup_{i=1}^{N}S_{\sigma}({\bm{X}_{i}}).</annotation></semantics></math> Then the coverage probability satisfies</span></p>
<table id="S4.Ex7" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="S4.Ex7X"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex7X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{P}(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in\mathcal{U}_{\sigma})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{P}(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in\mathcal{U}_{\sigma})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex7X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\geq\mathbb{E}\!\left[\Phi_{d,c}\!\left(\frac{d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(\bm{X})}{\sigma}\right)\right]," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>σ</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\geq\mathbb{E}\!\left[\Phi_{d,c}\!\left(\frac{d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(\bm{X})}{\sigma}\right)\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="S4.Ex7Xa"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex7Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathbb{P}(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in\mathcal{U}_{\sigma})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathbb{P}(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in\mathcal{U}_{\sigma})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S4.Ex7Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\leq 2e^{-c}+N\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\Phi_{d,c}\!\left(\frac{\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}^{\prime}\|}{\sigma}\right)\right]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>σ</mi></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\leq 2e^{-c}+N\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\Phi_{d,c}\!\left(\frac{\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}^{\prime}\|}{\sigma}\right)\right]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> is an independent copy of <math id="S4.Thmtheorem8.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐗</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS1.p15" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p15.1" class="ltx_p">The two bounds in the theorem are governed by the distribution of pairwise distances in the data as well as the ambient dimension <math id="S4.SS1.p15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> reflected by <math id="S4.SS1.p15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi_{d,c}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{d,c}</annotation></semantics></math>. The lower bound actually provides a very accurate estimation empirically and one may directly use it as a proxy to estimate the coverage; see <a href="#A5.F6" title="In E.2 Empirical Shell Coverage on CIFAR-10 ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> for experimental results on CIFAR-10.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Characterization of the Noise Regimes</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With the two quantities of posterior weight and data coverage defined and explored, we are ready to characterize the noise regimes.
In <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> we plot two curves of the two quantities against noise levels, based on a 1k subset of the CIFAR-10 dataset.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Note that in <a href="#S3.F2" title="In 3 Empirical Investigation of Memorization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>,
<span id="S4.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span> exhibits a positive memorization ratio for noise levels range <math id="S4.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\in[0.6,12]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0.6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\in[0.6,12]</annotation></semantics></math>, which closely aligns with the transition interval observed in <a href="#S4.F3" title="In 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.
Based on all these observations, we now informally identify the three noise regimes as follows using the two quantities:</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17846v1/cifar10_1k_coverage_weight.svg" id="S4.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:405/210;" width="405" height="210"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S4.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S4.F3.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Gaussian shell coverage and max posterior weight on CIFAR-10.<span id="S4.F3.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
We plot empirical estimates of the Gaussian shell coverage <math id="S4.F3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{\sigma}(p,\mathcal{D})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{\sigma}(p,\mathcal{D})</annotation></semantics></math> and the max posterior weight <math id="S4.F3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\sigma}(\mathcal{D})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\sigma}(\mathcal{D})</annotation></semantics></math> as functions of the noise level <math id="S4.F3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, using a <math id="S4.F3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\mathrm{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\mathrm{k}</annotation></semantics></math> CIFAR-10 training subset and <math id="S4.F3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\mathrm{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\mathrm{k}</annotation></semantics></math> held-out test images. </span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Regime</span></th>
<th id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Posterior weight</span></th>
<th id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.1.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Shell coverage</span></th></tr>
</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S4.SS2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="S4.SS2.p3.1.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">High</span></td>
<td id="S4.SS2.p3.1.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Low</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.SS2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.SS2.p3.1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Medium noise</span></th>
<td id="S4.SS2.p3.1.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Phase transition</span></td>
<td id="S4.SS2.p3.1.3.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.3.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Phase transition</span></td></tr>

<td id="S4.SS2.p3.1.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.4.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">High</span></td>
<td id="S4.SS2.p3.1.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding-left:4.0pt;padding-right:4.0pt;"><span id="S4.SS2.p3.1.4.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">High</span></td></tr>
