<div id="A2.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma B.5</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℱ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ℙ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})</annotation></semantics></math> be a probability space supporting random vectors
<math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X},\bm{X}^{\prime}:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X},\bm{X}^{\prime}:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{Z}:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐙</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{Z}:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Assume <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐙</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})</annotation></semantics></math> and that <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝐙</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> is independent of <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\bm{X},\bm{X}^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\bm{X},\bm{X}^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>.
Define the noisy point <math id="A2.Thmtheorem5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}_{\sigma}:=\bm{X}+\sigma\bm{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐗</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐗</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐙</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}_{\sigma}:=\bm{X}+\sigma\bm{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> and the indicator</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex88" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<div id="A2.SS1.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text">Define</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS1.p11.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p11.2.1" class="ltx_text">Then <math id="A2.SS1.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U=\Psi(\bm{X},\bm{X}^{\prime},\bm{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>𝒁</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U=\Psi(\bm{X},\bm{X}^{\prime},\bm{Z})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p12.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p12.1.1" class="ltx_text">For fixed <math id="A2.SS1.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,x^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,x^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math>, by independence and the definition of <math id="A2.SS1.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\sigma}({x})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\sigma}({x})</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<div id="A2.SS1.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p13.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p13.1.1" class="ltx_text">By <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem4" title="Lemma B.4. ‣ B.1 Proof of ‣ Appendix B Gaussian Shell and Coverage ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.4</span></a>, this probability depends

<div id="A2.SS1.p14" class="ltx_para">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p14.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p14.2.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS1.p15" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p15.1" class="ltx_p">Now we are ready to prove our theorem.</p>
</div>

<div id="A2.SS1.p18" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p18.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p18.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now consider the conditional expectation with respect to
<math id="A2.SS1.p18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X},\bm{X}_{i^{\star}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><msup><mi>i</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X},\bm{X}_{i^{\star}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
By <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma B.5. ‣ B.1 Proof of ‣ Appendix B Gaussian Shell and Coverage ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a>,</span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex101.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathbf{1}_{\{\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in S_{\sigma}({\bm{X}})\cap S_{\sigma}({\bm{X}_{i^{\star}}})}\}\;\middle|\;\bm{X},\bm{X}_{i^{\star}}\right]=\Phi_{d,c}\!\left(\frac{\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}_{i^{\star}}\|}{\sigma}\right)=\Phi_{d,c}\!\left(\frac{d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(\bm{X})}{\sigma}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>[</mo><msub><mn>𝟏</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>∩</mo><mi>S</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><msup><mi>i</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="true">|</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><msup><mi>i</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup></msub><mo>]</mo><mo>=</mo><msub><mi By <a href="#A2.Thmtheorem5" title="Lemma B.5. ‣ B.1 Proof of ‣ Appendix B Gaussian Shell and Coverage ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Lemma</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.5</span></a> and the tower property,</span></p>

<p id="A2.SS1.p21.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p21.2.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A2.SS1.p21.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is independent of <math id="A2.SS1.p21.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝑿</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A2.SS1.p21.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}_{i}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{=}}\bm{X}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mover><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi></mover><msup><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}_{i}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{=}}\bm{X}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, this equals
<math id="A2.SS1.p21.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\Phi_{d,c}(\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}^{\prime}\|/\sigma)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\Phi_{d,c}(\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}^{\prime}\|/\sigma)]</annotation></semantics></math>.
Summing over <math id="A2.SS1.p21.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> and adding the bound on <math id="A2.SS1.p21.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{P}(E^{c})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>E</mi><mi>c</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{P}(E^{c})</annotation></semantics></math> yields</span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex108.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{P}(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in\mathcal{U}_{\sigma})\leq 2e^{-c}+N\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\Phi_{d,c}\!\left(\frac{\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}^{\prime}\|}{\sigma}\right)\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>σ</mi></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{P}(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in\mathcal{U}_{\sigma})\leq 2e^{-c}+N\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\Phi_{d,c}\!\left(\frac{\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}^{\prime}\|}{\sigma}\right)\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS1.p21.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS1.p21.3.1" class="ltx_text">which completes the proof.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Proof of <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem9" title="Theorem 4.9 (Informal theorem). ‣ 4.2.1 Small Noise Regime ‣ 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.9</span></a></h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We formalize that, when training is effectively restricted to disjoint Gaussian shells, the denoising objective is highly non-identifiable and admits infinitely many global optima.
To isolate what the objective does (and does not) constrain on each shell, we idealize the Gaussian corruption by replacing the radially concentrated law of <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> with a <em id="A2.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">uniform distribution</em> on the corresponding unit shell <math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}:\ r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d}\leq\|z\|\leq r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.778em">:</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>in</mi></msubsup><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>out</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}:=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^{d}:\ r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d}\leq\|z\|\leq r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem B.6</span></span><span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fix <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and a finite dataset <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}=\{x_{1},\dots,x_{N}\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}=\{x_{1},\dots,x_{N}\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{\sigma}({x_{i}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{\sigma}({x_{i}})</annotation></semantics></math> be the Gaussian shells from Section <a href="#S4.SS1" title="4.1 Key Players for Per-Noise-Level Memorizations ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>, and
assume they are pairwise disjoint:</span></p>

and consider the shell-only objective</span></p>

<p id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">over measurable <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then, there are infinitely many global minimizers: any <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> such that</span></p>

<p id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">is a minimizer, and <math id="A2.Thmtheorem6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> can be defined arbitrarily on

<div id="A2.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">We first note that <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\sigma}(m)\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\sigma}(m)\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> for every measurable <math id="A2.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> be any measurable map satisfying</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex112" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex112.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m(y)=x_{i}\quad\text{for all }y\in S_{\sigma}({x_{i}}),\ \ i=1,\dots,N." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mspace style="width:1em;" width="1em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mtext>for all </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m(y)=x_{i}\quad\text{for all }y\in S_{\sigma}({x_{i}}),\ \ i=1,\dots,N.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Then for every <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in[N]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in[N]</annotation></semantics></math> and every <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝒁</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\bm{Z}\|\in[r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d},r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝒁</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>in</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mi>out</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bm{Z}\|\in[r^{\mathrm{in}}_{c,d},r^{\mathrm{out}}_{c,d}]</annotation></semantics></math>, we again have
<math id="A2.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}+\sigma\bm{Z}\in S_{\sigma}({x_{i}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝒁</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}+\sigma\bm{Z}\in S_{\sigma}({x_{i}})</annotation></semantics></math> and therefore</span></p>
<table id="A2.Ex113" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A2.Ex113.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m(x_{i}+\sigma\bm{Z})=x_{i},\qquad\|m(x_{i}+\sigma\bm{Z})-x_{i}\|_{2}^{2}=0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝒁</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝒁</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m(x_{i}+\sigma\bm{Z})=x_{i},\qquad\|m(x_{i}+\sigma\bm{Z})-x_{i}\|_{2}^{2}=0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A2.SS2.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS2.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text">Taking expectation shows <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\sigma}(m)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\sigma}(m)=0</annotation></semantics></math>, hence every such <math id="A2.SS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math> is a global minimizer.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Denoiser Behavior at Large Noise Levels</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we prove Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem11" title="Theorem 4.11. ‣ 4.2.2 Large Noise Regime ‣ 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.11</span></a>. Instead of working with the <math id="A3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> parameter directly, we first work with a parameter <math id="A3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> from flow matching as already mentioned in <a href="#A1.SS2" title="A.2 Cosine Similarity Concentration ‣ Appendix A Posterior Concentration and Cosine Similarity Concentration ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A.2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We use <math id="A3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}\sim p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}\sim p</annotation></semantics></math> to denote a random variable. Since we have assumed <math id="A3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> to have bounded support, we further assume that there is <math id="A3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>R</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that
<math id="A3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{supp}(p)\subset B_{R}(0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>supp</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊂</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{supp}(p)\subset B_{R}(0)</annotation></semantics></math>. We next rewrite the denoiser <math id="A3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> (cf. <a href="#A1.E22" title="In A.2 Cosine Similarity Concentration ‣ Appendix A Posterior Concentration and Cosine Similarity Concentration ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqn.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a>) as follows.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For <math id="A3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in(-1,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in(-1,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, define</p>

<p id="A3.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Then, we have that for any <math id="A3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math></p>

<p id="A3.p3.3" class="ltx_p">Note that although <math id="A3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\bm{X}\mid\bm{X}_{t}=x]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\bm{X}\mid\bm{X}_{t}=x]</annotation></semantics></math> is only defined for <math id="A3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in[0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in[0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, the formula <math id="A3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{t}(x)/D_{t}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{t}(x)/D_{t}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is well-defined for all <math id="A3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in(-1,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in(-1,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, and we will work with this extension of <math id="A3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> in the proof.
Note that <math id="A3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;W_{t}(y;x)\leq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;W_{t}(y;x)\leq 1</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A3.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in(-1,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in(-1,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A3.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{t}(x)\in(0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{t}(x)\in(0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We begin by establishing a collection of lemmas that will be used in the proof of <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem11" title="Theorem 4.11. ‣ 4.2.2 Large Noise Regime ‣ 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.11</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma C.1</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Fix <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then for every <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> the functions</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex114" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex114.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\longmapsto D_{t}(x),\qquad t\longmapsto N_{t}(x)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">⟼</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\longmapsto D_{t}(x),\qquad t\longmapsto N_{t}(x)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">are <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-\delta,\delta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-\delta,\delta]</annotation></semantics></math>.
Moreover, for <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=0,1,2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=0,1,2</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex115" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex115.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,t)\longmapsto\partial_{t}^{k}D_{t}(x),\qquad(x,t)\longmapsto\partial_{t}^{k}N_{t}(x)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em" stretchy="false">⟼</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∂</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em" stretchy="false">⟼</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∂</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,t)\longmapsto\partial_{t}^{k}D_{t}(x),\qquad(x,t)\longmapsto\partial_{t}^{k}N_{t}(x)</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">are continuous on <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}\times[-\delta,\delta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}\times[-\delta,\delta]</annotation></semantics></math>.
Moreover,</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex116" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">is continuous on <math id="A3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}\times[-\delta,\delta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}\times[-\delta,\delta]</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<div id="A3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Write</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex117" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex117.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{t}(y;x)=e^{F(t,x,y)},\qquad F(t,x,y)=-\frac{\|x-ty\|^{2}}{2(1-t)^{2}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msup></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{t}(y;x)=e^{F(t,x,y)},\qquad F(t,x,y)=-\frac{\|x-ty\|^{2}}{2(1-t)^{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p5.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text">The function <math id="A3.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> is smooth on <math id="A3.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(-1,1)\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-1,1)\times\mathbb{R}^{d}\times\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For <math id="A3.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=0,1,2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=0,1,2</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex118" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex118.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(y;x)=P_{k}(x,y,t)\,W_{t}(y;x)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∂</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(y;x)=P_{k}(x,y,t)\,W_{t}(y;x),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p5.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p5.3.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="A3.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is rational in <math id="A3.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> with the denominators of the form <math id="A3.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1-t)^{-m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1-t)^{-m}</annotation></semantics></math>, and polynomial in <math id="A3.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Fix <math id="A3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Since <math id="A3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|t|\leq\delta&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|t|\leq\delta&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, the factors <math id="A3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1-t)^{-m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1-t)^{-m}</annotation></semantics></math> are uniformly bounded.
Hence there exists <math id="A3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex119" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex119.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sup_{\begin{subarray}{c}\|x\|\leq a\\
|t|\leq\delta\\
\|y\|\leq R\end{subarray}}|\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(y;x)|\leq C." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">sup</mo><mtable rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></munder><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo lspace="0em">∂</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sup_{\begin{subarray}{c}\|x\|\leq a\\
|t|\leq\delta\\
\|y\|\leq R\end{subarray}}|\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(y;x)|\leq C.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A3.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">Because <math id="A3.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\bm{X}\|\leq R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bm{X}\|\leq R</annotation></semantics></math> a.s., we obtain</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex120" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex120.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="|\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(\bm{X};x)|\leq C,\qquad\|\bm{X}\,\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(\bm{X};x)\|\leq RC\quad\text{a.s.}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mo>∂</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo lspace="0.167em">≤</mo><mi>C</mi><mo rspace="1.889em">,</mo><mo rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><msubsup><mo>∂</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">∥</mo><mo lspace="0.0835em">≤</mo><mi>R</mi><mi>C</mi><mtext>a.s.</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(\bm{X};x)|\leq C,\qquad\|\bm{X}\,\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(\bm{X};x)\|\leq RC\quad\text{a.s.}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A3.p6.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p6.3.1" class="ltx_text">By dominated convergence,</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex121" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex121.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial_{t}^{k}D_{t}(x)=\mathbb{E}[\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(\bm{X};x)],\qquad\partial_{t}^{k}N_{t}(x)=\mathbb{E}[\bm{X}\,\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(\bm{X};x)]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∂</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo lspace="0em">∂</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.000em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mo>∂</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∂</mo><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial_{t}^{k}D_{t}(x)=\mathbb{E}[\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(\bm{X};x)],\qquad\partial_{t}^{k}N_{t}(x)=\mathbb{E}[\bm{X}\,\partial_{t}^{k}W_{t}(\bm{X};x)],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p6.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p6.4.1" class="ltx_text">and these depend continuously on <math id="A3.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,t)</annotation></semantics></math>.
We have <math id="A3.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t}(x)=N_{t}(x)/D_{t}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t}(x)=N_{t}(x)/D_{t}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{t}(x)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{t}(x)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Since <math id="A3.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> are <math id="A3.p6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="A3.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> with continuous derivatives.
The quotient rule gives the claim that <math id="A3.p6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial_{t}^{2}m_{t}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo>∂</mo><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial_{t}^{2}m_{t}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on <math id="A3.p6.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}\times[-\delta,\delta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}\times[-\delta,\delta]</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Now let <math id="A3.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu:=\mathbb{E}[\bm{X}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu:=\mathbb{E}[\bm{X}]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma:=\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{X})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>Cov</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma:=\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{X})</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="A3.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G=\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G=\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> and define
<math id="A3.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t}^{G}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t}^{G}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> by the same formula <a href="#A3.E31" title="In Appendix C Denoiser Behavior at Large Noise Levels ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqn.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">31</span></a>–<a href="#A3.E32" title="In Appendix C Denoiser Behavior at Large Noise Levels ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqn.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">32</span></a> but with expectation taken under <math id="A3.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>G</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Recall from <a href="#S4.E7" title="In 4.2.2 Large Noise Regime ‣ 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqn.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> that in the Gaussian case
<math id="A3.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A3.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma\succeq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⪰</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma\succeq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, we have a closed-form
expression for <math id="A3.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{\sigma}^{G}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{\sigma}^{G}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Using <a href="#A1.E23" title="In A.2 Cosine Similarity Concentration ‣ Appendix A Posterior Concentration and Cosine Similarity Concentration ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqn.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>, this yields the following
closed form for <math id="A3.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t}^{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t}^{G}</annotation></semantics></math> for every <math id="A3.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\in(-1,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\in(-1,1)</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A3.E33" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t}^{G}(x)=\mu+t\,\Sigma\bigl(t^{2}\Sigma+(1-t)^{2}I\bigr)^{-1}(x-t\,\mu)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t}^{G}(x)=\mu+t\,\Sigma\bigl(t^{2}\Sigma+(1-t)^{2}I\bigr)^{-1}(x-t\,\mu).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(33)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p8.2" class="ltx_p">This formula follows from the conditional mean formula for multivariate
Gaussian distributions.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Then it is not hard to prove the following lemma.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma C.2</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Gaussian smoothness of <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t}^{G}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t}^{G}</annotation></semantics></math>)<span id="A3.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For each fixed <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>, the map
<math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\mapsto m_{t}^{G}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\mapsto m_{t}^{G}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(-1,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-1,1)</annotation></semantics></math>. Moreover,
for any <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and any <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, the map <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,t)\mapsto m_{t}^{G}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,t)\mapsto m_{t}^{G}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math>
on <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{a}(0)\times[-\delta,\delta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{a}(0)\times[-\delta,\delta]</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma C.3</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For every fixed <math id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex122" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex122.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{0}(x)=\mu,\qquad\left.\frac{d}{dt}m_{t}(x)\right|_{t=0}=\Sigma x." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{0}(x)=\mu,\qquad\left.\frac{d}{dt}m_{t}(x)\right|_{t=0}=\Sigma x.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The same identities hold for <math id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t}^{G}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t}^{G}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> (with the same <math id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu,\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu,\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>).</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A3.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text">At <math id="A3.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=0</annotation></semantics></math>, the weight is constant in <math id="A3.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex123" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex123.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="W_{0}(y;x)=\exp(-\|x\|^{2}/2)=:W_{0}(x)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>exp</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">−</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∥</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em">/</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{0}(y;x)=\exp(-\|x\|^{2}/2)=:W_{0}(x).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p10.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p10.2.1" class="ltx_text">Therefore <math id="A3.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{0}(x)=W_{0}(x)\mathbb{E}[\bm{X}]=W_{0}(x)\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{0}(x)=W_{0}(x)\mathbb{E}[\bm{X}]=W_{0}(x)\mu</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{0}(x)=W_{0}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{0}(x)=W_{0}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>, giving <math id="A3.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{0}(x)=\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{0}(x)=\mu</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p11" class="ltx_para">

<div id="A3.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem C.4</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Assume that <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{supp}(p)\subset B_{R}(0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>supp</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊂</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{supp}(p)\subset B_{R}(0)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then for all <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math>, there exists a bounded function</span></p>

<p id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">such that for all <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\overline{B_{R}(0)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\overline{B_{R}(0)}</annotation></semantics></math> and all <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|t|\leq\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|t|\leq\delta</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<div id="A3.4" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A3.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p12.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p12.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="A3.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in\overline{B_{R}(0)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in\overline{B_{R}(0)}</annotation></semantics></math>, define</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex129" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex129.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{x}(t):=m_{t}(x)-m_{t}^{G}(x)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{x}(t):=m_{t}(x)-m_{t}^{G}(x).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A3.p12.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p12.2.1" class="ltx_text">By Lemma <a href="#A3.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma C.1. ‣ Appendix C Denoiser Behavior at Large Noise Levels ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a>, the function <math id="A3.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{x}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{x}</annotation></semantics></math> is of class <math id="A3.p12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="A3.p12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>.
Moreover, Lemma <a href="#A3.Thmtheorem3" title="Lemma C.3. ‣ Appendix C Denoiser Behavior at Large Noise Levels ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.3</span></a> implies that</span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex130.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{x}(0)=f_{x}^{\prime}(0)=0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{x}(0)=f_{x}^{\prime}(0)=0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A3.p12.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p12.3.1" class="ltx_text">Again by Lemma <a href="#A3.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma C.1. ‣ Appendix C Denoiser Behavior at Large Noise Levels ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.1</span></a>, the map <math id="A3.p12.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,t)\mapsto f_{x}^{\prime\prime}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,t)\mapsto f_{x}^{\prime\prime}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on
<math id="A3.p12.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{B_{R}(0)}\times[-\delta,\delta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{B_{R}(0)}\times[-\delta,\delta]</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p13.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p13.1.1" class="ltx_text">Define</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex131" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">
