</table>
<p id="A3.p13.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p13.2.1" class="ltx_text">Then the map <math id="A3.p13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,t,s)\mapsto(1-s)f_{x}^{\prime\prime}(st)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,t,s)\mapsto(1-s)f_{x}^{\prime\prime}(st)</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on the compact set</span></p>

<p id="A3.p13.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p13.3.1" class="ltx_text">and therefore <math id="A3.p13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{H}</annotation></semantics></math> is continuous on
<math id="A3.p13.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{B_{R}(0)}\times[-\delta,\delta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{B_{R}(0)}\times[-\delta,\delta]</annotation></semantics></math>.
By compactness, <math id="A3.p13.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{H}</annotation></semantics></math> is uniformly bounded on this set.</span></p>

<div id="A3.p14" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p14.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p14.1.1" class="ltx_text">Applying Taylor’s theorem with integral remainder, we obtain for all
<math id="A3.p14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|t|\leq\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|t|\leq\delta</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex133.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{x}(t)=t^{2}\int_{0}^{1}(1-s)f_{x}^{\prime\prime}(st)\,ds=t^{2}\tilde{H}(x,t)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0em">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>′′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{x}(t)=t^{2}\int_{0}^{1}(1-s)f_{x}^{\prime\prime}(st)\,ds=t^{2}\tilde{H}(x,t).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A3.p14.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p14.2.1" class="ltx_text">Consequently,</span></p>

<div id="A3.p15" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p15.1" class="ltx_p">Now, we are going to translate the second-order expansion in the small parameter <math id="A3.p15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> into an asymptotic expansion in terms of the scale parameter <math id="A3.p15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<div id="A3.5" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem11" title="Theorem 4.11. ‣ 4.2.2 Large Noise Regime ‣ 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.11</span></a>.</h6>
<div id="A3.p16" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p16.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p16.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A3.p16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma=\frac{1-t}{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mi>t</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma=\frac{1-t}{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, then, by <a href="#A1.E23" title="In A.2 Cosine Similarity Concentration ‣ Appendix A Posterior Concentration and Cosine Similarity Concentration ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqn.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a> we have that</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex135" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex135.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{\sigma}(x)=m_{t}(tx),\qquad m_{\sigma}^{G}(x)=m_{t}^{G}(tx)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{\sigma}(x)=m_{t}(tx),\qquad m_{\sigma}^{G}(x)=m_{t}^{G}(tx).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<table id="A3.Ex136" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex136.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t}(x)=m_{t}^{G}(x)+t^{2}\tilde{H}(x,t)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t}(x)=m_{t}^{G}(x)+t^{2}\tilde{H}(x,t).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p16.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p16.3.1" class="ltx_text">Replacing <math id="A3.p16.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="A3.p16.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="tx" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">tx</annotation></semantics></math>, we obtain</span></p>

</table>
<p id="A3.p16.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p16.4.1" class="ltx_text">By the relationship between <math id="A3.p16.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.p16.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>

<div id="A3.p17" class="ltx_para">

<p id="A3.p17.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p17.2.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A3.p17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=\frac{1}{1+\sigma}\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=\frac{1}{1+\sigma}\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A3.p17.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, there exists <math id="A3.p17.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{0}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{0}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that
<math id="A3.p17.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|t(\sigma)|\leq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|t(\sigma)|\leq 1</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A3.p17.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\geq\sigma_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\geq\sigma_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p18" class="ltx_para">
<table id="A3.Ex140" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex140.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|tx\|\leq\|x\|\leq R," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>R</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|tx\|\leq\|x\|\leq R,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.p18.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p18.1.1" class="ltx_text">so <math id="A3.p18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="tx\in\overline{B_{R}(0)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">tx\in\overline{B_{R}(0)}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p19" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p19.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p19.1.1" class="ltx_text">Therefore, for <math id="A3.p19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\geq\sigma_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\geq\sigma_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A3.p19.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(tx,t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(tx,t)</annotation></semantics></math> lies in
<math id="A3.p19.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{B_{R}(0)}\times[-\delta,\delta]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{B_{R}(0)}\times[-\delta,\delta]</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A3.p19.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{H}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>H</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{H}</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded.
Hence <math id="A3.p19.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded on
<math id="A3.p19.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\overline{B_{R}(0)}\times[\sigma_{0},\infty)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>R</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>σ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\overline{B_{R}(0)}\times[\sigma_{0},\infty)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.p20" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p20.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.p20.1.1" class="ltx_text">Finally, since <math id="A3.p20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=(1+\sigma)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=(1+\sigma)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="A3.p20.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{2}=(1+\sigma)^{-2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{2}=(1+\sigma)^{-2}</annotation></semantics></math>,
which yields the stated form.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Sensitivity Localization</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We analyze the case when the data distribution <math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is a Gaussian distribution <math id="A4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="A4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> to establish a spatial sensitivity decay control. Recall from <a href="#S4.E7" title="In 4.2.2 Large Noise Regime ‣ 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eqn.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> that the optimal denoiser for <math id="A4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> is given by the closed-form</p>
<table id="A4.Ex141" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex141.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{\sigma}(x)=\mu+\Sigma(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}(x-\mu)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{\sigma}(x)=\mu+\Sigma(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}(x-\mu).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In the following we only consider the case of a single channel.
The multivariate case can be handled by the same arguments by treating each channel separately.
We think of <math id="A4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=r\times r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=r\times r</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="A4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is the resolution and then each dimension represents a single-valued pixel.
To quantify how much the denoiser at pixel <math id="A4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> depends on observation <math id="A4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, we
study the Jacobian <math id="A4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{x}m_{\sigma}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>x</mi></msub><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{x}m_{\sigma}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>.
By Tweedie’s formula <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>, we have that</p>
<table id="A4.Ex142" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex142.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{x}m_{\sigma}(x)=\frac{1}{\sigma^{2}}\,\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{X}\mid\bm{X}_{\sigma}=x)=\Sigma(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>x</mi></msub><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Cov</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{x}m_{\sigma}(x)=\frac{1}{\sigma^{2}}\,\mathrm{Cov}(\bm{X}\mid\bm{X}_{\sigma}=x)=\Sigma(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p2.2" class="ltx_p">The expression for <math id="A4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{x}m_{\sigma}(y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>x</mi></msub><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{x}m_{\sigma}(y)</annotation></semantics></math> was derived in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite>, who also observed that <math id="A4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{x}m_{\sigma}(y)\to I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>x</mi></msub><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{x}m_{\sigma}(y)\to I</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
However, convergence to the identity does not by itself characterize how the off-diagonal entries decay with spatial distance.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We now make the spatial decay claim precise under cyclic stationary.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma D.1</span></span><span id="A4.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any <math id="A4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\neq j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\neq j</annotation></semantics></math>, we have that</span></p>
<table id="A4.E35" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E35.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|\frac{\partial[m_{\sigma}]_{i}}{\partial x_{j}}\right|=\sigma^{2}\left|[(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}]_{ij}\right|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{\partial[m_{\sigma}]_{i}}{\partial x_{j}}\right|=\sigma^{2}\left|[(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}]_{ij}\right|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(35)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">The identity (<a href="#A4.E35" title="Eqn. 35 ‣ Lemma D.1. ‣ Appendix D Sensitivity Localization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">35</span></a>) follows from the simple identity
<math id="A4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}=I-\sigma^{2}(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}=I-\sigma^{2}(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> and the fact that <math id="A4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{ij}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{ij}=0</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="A4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\neq j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\neq j</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition D.2</span></span><span id="A4.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Circulant covariance)<span id="A4.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A matrix <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> is called <em id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">circulant</em> if there exists a vector
<math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=[c_{0},\dots,c_{d-1}]^{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>T</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=[c_{0},\dots,c_{d-1}]^{T}</annotation></semantics></math> such that</p>
<table id="A4.Ex143" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex143.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{ij}=c_{(i-j)\bmod d},\qquad i,j\in\{0,\dots,d-1\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{ij}=c_{(i-j)\bmod d},\qquad i,j\in\{0,\dots,d-1\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Equivalently, each row of <math id="A4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is a cyclic shift of its first row.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma D.3</span></span><span id="A4.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> be circulant and let
<math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega=e^{2\pi i/d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega=e^{2\pi i/d}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is diagonalized by the discrete Fourier
basis <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\omega^{jk})_{j,k=0}^{d-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\omega^{jk})_{j,k=0}^{d-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, with eigenvalues
<math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\lambda_{k})_{k=0}^{d-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\lambda_{k})_{k=0}^{d-1}</annotation></semantics></math>. In particular, for any function <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>f</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f</annotation></semantics></math> applied
spectrally to <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, the matrix <math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> is circulant and its entries depend only on the wrap-around distance
<math id="A4.Thmtheorem3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{dist}(i,j):=\min\{|i-j|,\,d-|i-j|\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>dist</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{dist}(i,j):=\min\{|i-j|,\,d-|i-j|\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof sketch.</h6>
<div id="A4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">This is a classical property of circulant matrices: they are simultaneously
diagonalized by the discrete Fourier transform, and functional calculus
preserves circulant structure. See <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite> for a detailed
treatment of the spectral theory of circulant and Toeplitz matrices.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem D.4</span></span><span id="A4.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Assume <math id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is circulant. Let <math id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega=e^{2\pi i/d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ω</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega=e^{2\pi i/d}</annotation></semantics></math> and let <math id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\lambda_{k})_{k=0}^{d-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\lambda_{k})_{k=0}^{d-1}</annotation></semantics></math> be the
eigenvalues of <math id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> in the discrete Fourier basis (Lemma <a href="#A4.Thmtheorem3" title="Lemma D.3. ‣ Appendix D Sensitivity Localization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.3</span></a>). Define</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex144" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex144.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{k}:=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{\lambda_{k}+\sigma^{2}},\qquad q_{r}:=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}h_{k}\,\omega^{rk},\qquad r\in\{0,\dots,d-1\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>d</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{k}:=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{\lambda_{k}+\sigma^{2}},\qquad q_{r}:=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}h_{k}\,\omega^{rk},\qquad r\in\{0,\dots,d-1\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For all <math id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\neq j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\neq j</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n:=\min\{|i-j|,\,d-|i-j|\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n:=\min\{|i-j|,\,d-|i-j|\}</annotation></semantics></math> be the wrap-around distance. Then,</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex145" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex145.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|\frac{\partial[m_{\sigma}]_{i}}{\partial x_{j}}\right|=|q_{n}|." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{\partial[m_{\sigma}]_{i}}{\partial x_{j}}\right|=|q_{n}|.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Moreover, for all <math id="A4.Thmtheorem4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\in\{1,\dots,\lfloor d/2\rfloor\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌊</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⌋</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\in\{1,\dots,\lfloor d/2\rfloor\}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="A4.E36" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E36.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\left|\frac{\partial[m_{\sigma}]_{i}}{\partial x_{j}}\right|\leq\frac{\mathrm{TV}(h)}{4n},\qquad\mathrm{TV}(h):=\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}|h_{k+1}-h_{k}|\ \ (\text{indices mod }d)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em">|</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="false">|</mo><mo lspace="0.167em">≤</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>TV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>TV</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">:=</mo><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">indices mod </mtext><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{\partial[m_{\sigma}]_{i}}{\partial x_{j}}\right|\leq\frac{\mathrm{TV}(h)}{4n},\qquad\mathrm{TV}(h):=\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}|h_{k+1}-h_{k}|\ \ (\text{indices mod }d).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(36)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>

<div id="A4.4" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A4.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Define the matrix</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex146" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex146.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\sigma}:=\sigma^{2}(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\sigma}:=\sigma^{2}(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A4.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> is circulant, so is <math id="A4.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I</annotation></semantics></math>, and hence <math id="A4.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="A4.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> are circulant as well (Lemma <a href="#A4.Thmtheorem3" title="Lemma D.3. ‣ Appendix D Sensitivity Localization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.3</span></a> applied to the spectral
function <math id="A4.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(t)=1/(t+\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(t)=1/(t+\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>). In the DFT basis, the eigenvalues of <math id="A4.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> are</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex147" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex147.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="h_{k}=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{\lambda_{k}+\sigma^{2}},\qquad k=0,\dots,d-1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{k}=\frac{\sigma^{2}}{\lambda_{k}+\sigma^{2}},\qquad k=0,\dots,d-1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p6.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p6.3.1" class="ltx_text">Therefore <math id="A4.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> has circulant kernel <math id="A4.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(q_{r})_{r=0}^{d-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(q_{r})_{r=0}^{d-1}</annotation></semantics></math> given by the inverse DFT:</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex148" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex148.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[Q_{\sigma}]_{ij}=q_{(i-j)\bmod d},\qquad q_{r}=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}h_{k}\,\omega^{rk}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>mod</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>d</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[Q_{\sigma}]_{ij}=q_{(i-j)\bmod d},\qquad q_{r}=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}h_{k}\,\omega^{rk}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</div>
<div id="A4.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now fix <math id="A4.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\neq j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\neq j</annotation></semantics></math> and let <math id="A4.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n:=\min\{|i-j|,\,d-|i-j|\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n:=\min\{|i-j|,\,d-|i-j|\}</annotation></semantics></math>. By Lemma <a href="#A4.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma D.1. ‣ Appendix D Sensitivity Localization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D.1</span></a>,</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex149" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex149.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|\frac{\partial[m_{\sigma}]_{i}}{\partial x_{j}}\right|=\sigma^{2}\left|[(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}]_{ij}\right|=\left|[Q_{\sigma}]_{ij}\right|=|q_{n}|," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\frac{\partial[m_{\sigma}]_{i}}{\partial x_{j}}\right|=\sigma^{2}\left|[(\Sigma+\sigma^{2}I)^{-1}]_{ij}\right|=\left|[Q_{\sigma}]_{ij}\right|=|q_{n}|,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
