</table>
<p id="A4.p7.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p7.2.1" class="ltx_text">which proves the first claim.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A4.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">For the decay bound, let <math id="A4.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\Delta h)_{k}:=h_{k+1}-h_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\Delta h)_{k}:=h_{k+1}-h_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> (indices modulo <math id="A4.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>). For <math id="A4.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\not\equiv 0\pmod{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>≢</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mspace style="width:0.949em;" width="0.949em"></mspace><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">mod</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\not\equiv 0\pmod{d}</annotation></semantics></math>,
a cyclic summation-by-parts identity (discrete integration by parts) yields</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex150" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex150.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{n}=\frac{\omega^{n}}{d(1-\omega^{n})}\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}(\Delta h)_{k}\,\omega^{nk}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>ω</mi><mi>n</mi></msup><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></munderover><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{n}=\frac{\omega^{n}}{d(1-\omega^{n})}\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}(\Delta h)_{k}\,\omega^{nk}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p8.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p8.2.1" class="ltx_text">Taking absolute values and using the triangle inequality gives</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex151" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex151.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|q_{n}|\leq\frac{\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}|\Delta h_{k}|}{d\,|1-\omega^{n}|}=\frac{\mathrm{TV}(h)}{d\,|1-\omega^{n}|}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mfrac><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>TV</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|q_{n}|\leq\frac{\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}|\Delta h_{k}|}{d\,|1-\omega^{n}|}=\frac{\mathrm{TV}(h)}{d\,|1-\omega^{n}|}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p8.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p8.3.1" class="ltx_text">Finally, for <math id="A4.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\leq n\leq d/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\leq n\leq d/2</annotation></semantics></math> we have</span></p>
<table id="A4.Ex152" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.Ex152.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|1-\omega^{n}|=2|\sin(\pi n/d)|\geq\frac{4n}{d}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mi>d</mi></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|1-\omega^{n}|=2|\sin(\pi n/d)|\geq\frac{4n}{d},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.p8.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.p8.4.1" class="ltx_text">and substituting into the previous display yields (<a href="#A4.E36" title="Eqn. 36 ‣ Theorem D.4. ‣ Appendix D Sensitivity Localization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">36</span></a>).
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Experiment Details</h2>

<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Sampling Schedule</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unless otherwise specified, the sampling schedule used in our experiments is the polynomial sampling schedule from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>:</p>
<table id="A5.Ex153" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.Ex153.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{i}=\Big(\sigma_{\max}^{1/\rho}+\frac{i}{N-1}\big(\sigma_{\min}^{1/\rho}-\sigma_{\max}^{1/\rho}\big)\Big)^{\rho}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>i</mi><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow><mi>ρ</mi></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{i}=\Big(\sigma_{\max}^{1/\rho}+\frac{i}{N-1}\big(\sigma_{\min}^{1/\rho}-\sigma_{\max}^{1/\rho}\big)\Big)^{\rho},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">for <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=0,\ldots,N-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=0,\ldots,N-1</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\max}=80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\max}=80</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\min}=0.002" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.002</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\min}=0.002</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=18" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=18</annotation></semantics></math> is a popular choice for sampling on CIFAR-10.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.2 </span>Empirical Shell Coverage on CIFAR-10</h3>

<figure id="A5.F6" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17846v1/figures/cifar10_shell_bounds.png" id="A5.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:333/222;" width="333" height="222" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="A5.F6.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="A5.F6.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Empirical shell coverage on CIFAR-10.</span> We plot the lower bound, coverage, and upper bound from Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem8" title="Theorem 4.8. ‣ 4.1 Key Players for Per-Noise-Level Memorizations ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.8</span></a>.
The lower bound curve (blue) is nearly indistinguishable from the coverage curve across the entire range of <math id="A5.F6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, as it almost perfectly overlaps with it.
</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We empirically evaluate the lower and upper bounds in <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem8" title="Theorem 4.8. ‣ 4.1 Key Players for Per-Noise-Level Memorizations ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.8</span></a> and compare them with the Gaussian shell coverage probability on the CIFAR-10 dataset; see <a href="#A5.F6" title="In E.2 Empirical Shell Coverage on CIFAR-10 ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figure</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>.
All images are flattened to vectors in <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=3072" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3072</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=3072</annotation></semantics></math> and linearly rescaled to lie in <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1,1]^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1,1]^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For a fixed shell width parameter <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c=5</annotation></semantics></math>, we estimate the function</p>
<table id="A5.Ex154" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A5.Ex154.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi_{d,c}(t)=\mathbb{P}\!\left(\|\bm{Z}\|\in[a_{d},b_{d}],\;\|\bm{Z}+te_{1}\|\in[a_{d},b_{d}]\right),\qquad\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.441em;" width="0.441em"><mi>ℙ</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>𝒁</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝒁</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>𝒁</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{d,c}(t)=\mathbb{P}\!\left(\|\bm{Z}\|\in[a_{d},b_{d}],\;\|\bm{Z}+te_{1}\|\in[a_{d},b_{d}]\right),\qquad\bm{Z}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_{d}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A5.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">using Monte Carlo with <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>5000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5000</annotation></semantics></math> i.i.d. Gaussian samples.
We reuse the same Gaussian samples to evaluate <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi_{d,c}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{d,c}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> for all values of <math id="A5.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> encountered in the experiment.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Noise schedule.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the EDM polynomial noise schedule stated in <a href="#A5.SS1" title="E.1 Sampling Schedule ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.1</span></a> with <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\max}=80" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>80</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\max}=80</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\min}=0.002" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.002</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\min}=0.002</annotation></semantics></math>, and a 40-step discretization (<math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=40" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=40</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Upper bound.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To estimate the upper bound term
<math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N\,\mathbb{E}[\Phi_{d,c}(\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}^{\prime}\|/\sigma)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\,\mathbb{E}[\Phi_{d,c}(\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}^{\prime}\|/\sigma)]</annotation></semantics></math>
with <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=1000</annotation></semantics></math>, we independently sample <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12,000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12{,}000</annotation></semantics></math> pairs <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\bm{X},\bm{X}^{\prime})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\bm{X},\bm{X}^{\prime})</annotation></semantics></math> from the CIFAR-10 training set and compute the empirical average of <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi_{d,c}(\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}^{\prime}\|/\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{d,c}(\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}^{\prime}\|/\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> for each noise level <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Lower bound.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To estimate the lower bound term
<math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\Phi_{d,c}(d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(\bm{X})/\sigma)]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\Phi_{d,c}(d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(\bm{X})/\sigma)]</annotation></semantics></math>,
we perform <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="250" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>250</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">250</annotation></semantics></math> independent trials.
In each trial, we sample a fresh subset <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\bm{X}_{1},\dots,\bm{X}_{N}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\bm{X}_{1},\dots,\bm{X}_{N}\}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=1000</annotation></semantics></math> training images and independently sample <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>8</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> test images <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝑿</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For each test image, we compute the nearest-neighbor distance
<math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(\bm{X})=\min_{1\leq i\leq N}\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}_{i}\|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>min</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(\bm{X})=\min_{1\leq i\leq N}\|\bm{X}-\bm{X}_{i}\|</annotation></semantics></math>
and evaluate <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi_{d,c}(d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(\bm{X})/\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝑿</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>σ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi_{d,c}(d_{1\mathrm{NN}}(\bm{X})/\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The results are averaged over test images and trials.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Gaussian shell coverage.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We estimate the true coverage probability
<math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{P}(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in\mathcal{U}_{\sigma})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℙ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒰</mi><mi>σ</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{P}(\bm{X}_{\sigma}\in\mathcal{U}_{\sigma})</annotation></semantics></math>
using <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="350" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>350</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">350</annotation></semantics></math> independent trials.
In each trial, we sample a fresh subset <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\bm{X}_{1},\dots,\bm{X}_{N}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝑿</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\bm{X}_{1},\dots,\bm{X}_{N}\}</annotation></semantics></math> of size <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=1000</annotation></semantics></math> and an independent test image <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝑿</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For each noise level <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, we draw <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math> independent Gaussian noises <math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝒁</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{Z}</annotation></semantics></math> and check whether
<math id="A5.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bm{X}+\sigma\bm{Z}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝑿</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝒁</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bm{X}+\sigma\bm{Z}</annotation></semantics></math>
lies in at least one shell centered at the subset points.
The coverage probability is estimated by averaging over noises and trials.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.3 </span>Max vs Self Posterior Weight</h3>

<figure id="A5.F7" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17846v1/figures/posterior_weights_vs_sigma.png" id="A5.F7.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:333/222;" width="333" height="222" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 7</span>: </span><span id="A5.F7.5" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">
<span id="A5.F7.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Max vs. Sample Weight on 1K CIFAR-10.</span>
We plot average values of <math id="A5.F7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max_{1\leq i\leq N}w_{i}(x_{1}+\sigma\bm{Z},\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>max</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝒁</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max_{1\leq i\leq N}w_{i}(x_{1}+\sigma\bm{Z},\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.F7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{1}(x_{1}+\sigma\bm{Z})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝒁</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{1}(x_{1}+\sigma\bm{Z})</annotation></semantics></math> across a range of <math id="A5.F7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. The two curves show that the max posterior weight can usually be well estimated by the sample weight, particularly at smaller noise levels where they coincide.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Max vs Self weight estimation.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For each noise level <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>,
we fix a subset of <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N=1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N=1000</annotation></semantics></math> images sampled uniformly without replacement from the CIFAR-10 dataset. We then draw 100 base points without replacement from the subset and for each base point <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> we compute for each <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,\dots,N\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,\dots,N\}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{i}(x_{1}+\sigma z,\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{i}(x_{1}+\sigma z,\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> over 400 independent Gaussian noises <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>. We then compute the averages for both <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\max_{i}w_{i}(x_{1}+\sigma z,\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>max</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\max_{i}w_{i}(x_{1}+\sigma z,\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{1}(x_{1}+\sigma z,\sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{1}(x_{1}+\sigma z,\sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> over all base points <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and subsequent samples <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>. The resulting curves show the averages for each value of <math id="A5.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.4 </span>Danger Zone Identification: 2k Car Subset</h3>

<div id="A5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In Figure <a href="#A5.F8" title="Figure 8 ‣ E.4 Danger Zone Identification: 2k Car Subset ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, we overlay the coverage and max posterior weight curves from Figure <a href="#S4.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 4.2 Characterization of the Noise Regimes ‣ 4 Geometric Interpretation of Noise Regimes ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> for the 2k car training set and 1k car test set. The danger zone is identified as the region where both metrics are high, which in the case of <math id="A5.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2k</annotation></semantics></math>-car is a narrow interval containing the intersection point <math id="A5.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\approx 1.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\approx 1.9</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F8" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17846v1/car_coverage_weight.svg" id="A5.F8.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:333/173;" width="333" height="173"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F8.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 8</span>: </span><span id="A5.F8.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Coverage and max posterior weight vs noise level for 2k car training set and 1k car test set. The danger zone is where both metrics are high, spanning <math id="A5.F8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\in[1,5]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\in[1,5]</annotation></semantics></math> with intersection near <math id="A5.F8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\approx 1.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\approx 1.9</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.5 </span>Pareto Frontier of Training Configurations on 1024 Grayscale CelebA Images</h3>

<div id="A5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compute the FID score of 10k samples against 10k held out test images. We visualize the Pareto frontier of different timestep gap configurations on the 1024 grayscale CelebA training set in Figure <a href="#A5.F9" title="Figure 9 ‣ E.5 Pareto Frontier of Training Configurations on 1024 Grayscale CelebA Images ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>. Each point represents a different gap configuration, plotting FID score against memorization rate (FMEM%). The dashed line connects non-dominated solutions forming the Pareto frontier.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17846v1/figures/FINAL_pareto_v5.png" id="A5.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:405/289;" width="405" height="289" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F9.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="A5.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Pareto frontier showing the trade-off between image quality (FID) and memorization (FMEM%). Each point represents a different timestep gap configuration. The dashed line connects non-dominated solutions forming the Pareto frontier.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.6 </span>Denoiser Swapping Experiments</h3>

<div id="A5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To understand which noise levels are critical for sample quality, we perform denoiser swapping experiments. We generate samples using hybrid schedules that switch between <span id="A5.SS6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span> and <span id="A5.SS6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-50K</span> at different <math id="A5.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> regions (large: <math id="A5.SS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma&gt;5.3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>5.3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma&gt;5.3</annotation></semantics></math>, medium: <math id="A5.SS6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\in[0.06,5.3]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0.06</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5.3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\in[0.06,5.3]</annotation></semantics></math>, small: <math id="A5.SS6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma&lt;0.06" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>0.06</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma&lt;0.06</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F10" title="Figure 10 ‣ E.6 Denoiser Swapping Experiments ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> shows representative samples from each condition. Key findings:</p>
<ul id="A5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="A5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Swapping to <span id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-50K</span> in the <span id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">medium region</span> (steps 7-13) produces the largest quality improvement when starting from <span id="A5.I1.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Swapping to <span id="A5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span> in the <span id="A5.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">medium region</span> causes the largest quality degradation when starting from <span id="A5.I1.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-50K</span>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="A5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">large and small region swaps have minimal impact on final sample quality.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This confirms that the mid-<math id="A5.SS6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> region is where memorization most impacts generation quality, aligning with our one-step memorization analysis. Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Trajectory-Level memorization. ‣ 3 Empirical Investigation of Memorization ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> in the main text quantifies the memorization rates across all conditions.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F10" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17846v1/figures/sample_grid_with_danger_zone.png" id="A5.F10.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/328;" width="476" height="328" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F10.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 10</span>: </span><span id="A5.F10.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Denoiser Swapping Samples.<span id="A5.F10.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Top half: </span>EDM-1K<span id="A5.F10.9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> base with </span>EDM-50K<span id="A5.F10.9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> swapped in different regions. Bottom half: </span>EDM-50K<span id="A5.F10.9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> base with </span>EDM-1K<span id="A5.F10.9.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> swapped in. Red boxes indicate memorized samples (where <math id="A5.F10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{1\mathrm{NN}}&lt;d_{2\mathrm{NN}}/3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow></msub><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{1\mathrm{NN}}&lt;d_{2\mathrm{NN}}/3</annotation></semantics></math>). Swapping in the medium region (steps 6-13) completely flips memorization behavior, while swapping only in the danger zone (steps 7-10) shows partial effects.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>

<div id="A5.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the standard 18 steps of EDM for sampling with Euler method, the noise level <math id="A5.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> and step translation can be seen in <a href="#A5.SS7" title="E.7 One-Step Memorization Showcase ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Section</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E.7</span></a>.
Figures <a href="#A5.F11" title="Figure 11 ‣ E.7 One-Step Memorization Showcase ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>–<a href="#A5.F16" title="Figure 16 ‣ E.7 One-Step Memorization Showcase ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> visualize one-step denoising output at six different noise levels spanning the full diffusion schedule. Each figure shows, from top to bottom: the initial clean test image, noisy input, <span id="A5.SS7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-1K</span> output followed by its 1-NN in the training set, <span id="A5.SS7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EDM-50K</span> output followed by its 1-NN, and <span id="A5.SS7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">EMP-1K</span> output followed by its 1-NN.</p>
</div>

<section id="A5.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.8 </span>Detailed Memorization Visualizations for Gap Training</h3>

<div id="A5.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide detailed visualizations comparing the memorization behavior of the three anti-memorization methods evaluated in Section <a href="#S5" title="5 Targeted Noise Region Undertraining ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Each image pair is arranged as [Generated sample — 1-NN from training set], where the left image shows a generated sample and the right image shows its nearest neighbor from the 2,000-image training set. A yellow border around both images in a pair indicates that the sample is classified as memorized according to the criterion: <math id="A5.SS8.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|g-x_{\text{1-NN}}\|_{2}&lt;\|g-x_{\text{2-NN}}\|_{2}/3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mtext>1-NN</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mtext>2-NN</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|g-x_{\text{1-NN}}\|_{2}&lt;\|g-x_{\text{2-NN}}\|_{2}/3</annotation></semantics></math>.
Figures <a href="#A5.F17" title="Figure 17 ‣ E.8 Detailed Memorization Visualizations for Gap Training ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>, <a href="#A5.F18" title="Figure 18 ‣ E.8 Detailed Memorization Visualizations for Gap Training ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>, and <a href="#A5.F19" title="Figure 19 ‣ E.8 Detailed Memorization Visualizations for Gap Training ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a> show complete 8<math id="A5.SS8.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>8 grids with 64 generated samples for each method, enabling detailed assessment of memorization patterns.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F17" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17846v1/appendix_grid_baseline.png" id="A5.F17.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/216;" width="429" height="216" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F17.6" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 17</span>: </span><span id="A5.F17.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">2k-Baseline detailed visualization.<span id="A5.F17.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> This 8<math id="A5.F17.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>8 grid shows 64 image pairs, each arranged as [Generated — 1-NN from training]. In each pair, the generated sample appears on the <em id="A5.F17.7.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">left</em> and its nearest neighbor from the 2,000-image training set appears on the <em id="A5.F17.7.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">right</em>.
Red borders indicate memorized pairs. The high prevalence of red borders confirms severe memorization in the baseline case.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F18" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17846v1/appendix_grid_dummy.png" id="A5.F18.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/216;" width="429" height="216" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F18.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 18</span>: </span><span id="A5.F18.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">2k-Dummy detailed visualization.<span id="A5.F18.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Same layout as Figure <a href="#A5.F17" title="Figure 17 ‣ E.8 Detailed Memorization Visualizations for Gap Training ‣ Appendix E Experiment Details ‣ Two Calm Ends and the Wild Middle:A Geometric Picture of Memorization in Diffusion Models" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>: each of the 64 pairs shows [Generated — 1-NN]. Red borders mark memorized pairs. Conditional training with an auxiliary noise class substantially reduces memorization. Most generated samples now deviate meaningfully from their nearest neighbors, though several memorized samples remain (red borders).</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F19" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17846v1/appendix_grid_gap.png" id="A5.F19.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/216;" width="429" height="216" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F19.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 19</span>: </span><span id="A5.F19.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">2k-Gap detailed visualization.<span id="A5.F19.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> Same layout: 64 pairs of [Generated — 1-NN]. Gap training (excluding <math id="A5.F19.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma\in[1.0,5.0]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5.0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma\in[1.0,5.0]</annotation></semantics></math> from training) achieves minimal memorization. Generated samples maintain semantic similarity to cars while introducing novel variations in color, viewpoint, and detail. This demonstrates that targeted undertraining in the medium-<math id="A5.F19.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma</annotation></semantics></math> danger zone enables robust generalization.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS9" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.9 </span>Timestep Gap Configurations: Visual Comparisons</h3>

<div id="A5.SS9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Visual comparison of memorization behavior for different timestep gap configurations on 1024 grayscale CelebA samples. Each 4<math id="A5.SS9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>4 grid shows 16 image pairs arranged as [Generated — 1-NN from training]. Red borders indicate memorized samples according to the criterion: <math id="A5.SS9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|g-x_{\text{1-NN}}\|_{2}&lt;\|g-x_{\text{2-NN}}\|_{2}/3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mtext>1-NN</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mtext>2-NN</mtext></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|g-x_{\text{1-NN}}\|_{2}&lt;\|g-x_{\text{2-NN}}\|_{2}/3</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F20" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17846v1/figures/celeba_1024_baseline_grid.png" id="A5.F20.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/213;" width="429" height="213" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F20.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 20</span>: </span><span id="A5.F20.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Baseline (no gap).<span id="A5.F20.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> 74.97% memorization. The high prevalence of red borders confirms severe memorization in this low-data regime.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F21" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17846v1/figures/celeba_1024_gap_100_200_grid.png" id="A5.F21.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/213;" width="429" height="213" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F21.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 21</span>: </span><span id="A5.F21.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Gap [100–200].<span id="A5.F21.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> 42.93% memorization. Skipping 100 timesteps in the early danger zone reduces memorization substantially.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F22" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17846v1/figures/celeba_1024_gap_100_275_grid.png" id="A5.F22.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/213;" width="429" height="213" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F22.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 22</span>: </span><span id="A5.F22.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Gap [100–275].<span id="A5.F22.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> 13.45% memorization. Extending the gap further into the danger zone dramatically reduces memorization.</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A5.F23" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17846v1/figures/celeba_1024_gap_100_350_grid.png" id="A5.F23.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:429/213;" width="429" height="213" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A5.F23.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 23</span>: </span><span id="A5.F23.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:90%;">Gap [100–350].<span id="A5.F23.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> 9.24% memorization. The widest gap achieves the lowest memorization rate, though at the cost of increased FID (26.74 vs 13.09 baseline).</span></span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
